1.title: Text Analysis and Speech Applications
1.text: Welcome to Module ten: Text Analysis and Speech Applications. It covers the exam area Implement A I solutions by using Microsoft Foundry. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Build a lightweight application that includes text analysis. Respond to spoken prompts by using a deployed multimodal model. Build a lightweight application by using Azure Speech in Foundry Tools. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Implement A I solutions by using Microsoft Foundry (fifty-five to sixty percent). Exam format: a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes; check the exam page for the time. Validated against: the official A I nine oh one study guide, current skills measured.

1.title: A text analysis application
1.text: A text analysis application. To analyze text in code you use Azure Language through a client library. The pattern is the same as other Foundry Tools: a client with an endpoint and a credential, one call, read the result. one. Create the resource. A Language (Foundry Tool) resource gives an endpoint and a key. two. Create the client. Text Analytics Client with the endpoint and an Azure Key Credential. three. Send documents. A list of text strings. four. Call the feature. For example analyze sentiment. five. Read the result. Overall sentiment, sentence results, confidence scores.

1.title: A text analysis application, continued
1.text: A text analysis application. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: A text analysis app uses a key and endpoint (or Entra I D), a client object, and one method per feature. The method name tells the feature: analyze sentiment, extract key phrases, recognize entities, detect language. for the last three names.

1.title: A text analysis application, continued
1.text: A text analysis application. pip install azure ai textanalytics five dot two dot zero. The package used in the quickstart. os dot environ dot get... Reads the key and endpoint from environment variables, not from the code. Text Analytics Client... The client for text analysis features. documents... The input: a list of texts. analyze sentiment..., show opinion mining True. Sentiment plus opinions about specific targets. The sample result for that text is an overall sentiment of Mixed, with a result for each sentence. Other methods in the same client cover key phrase extraction, entity recognition, language detection and P I I detection. for current package names and versions.

1.title: Speech applications with Azure Speech
1.text: Speech applications with Azure Speech. Azure Speech in Foundry Tools gives speech recognition, speech synthesis and translation. In Python you use the Speech S D K package azure cognitiveservices speech. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Speech applications with Azure Speech, continued
1.text: Speech applications with Azure Speech. Speech Config subscription..., endpoint... Connects to the Speech resource with a key and endpoint. speech recognition language en U S. The spoken language to recognize. Audio Config use default microphone True. Where the audio comes from: the microphone. For a file use Audio Config filename Your Audio File dot wav. Speech Recognizer... The object that turns speech into text. recognize once async dot get. Recognizes one utterance (up to about thirty seconds, or until silence) and returns the result. For text to speech the S D K uses a speech synthesizer with a voice you choose, and S S M L can adjust pitch, rate and volume. for the class name. Exam tip: Audio Config says where audio comes from or goes to (microphone, speaker, file). Speech Config says which resource and language or voice. Recognizer equals speech to text; synthesizer equals text to speech.

1.title: Speech applications with Azure Speech, continued
1.text: Speech applications with Azure Speech. The figure shows this: Speech application: microphone or file to recognizer to text; text to synthesizer to audio.

1.title: Responding to spoken prompts with a multimodal model
1.text: Responding to spoken prompts with a multimodal model. A multimodal model can accept more than text: some deployed models accept audio (spoken prompts) as input and can reply in text or speech. There are two designs. Pipeline. How it works: Speech to text (Azure Speech) to text model to text to speech (Azure Speech). When: You want control of each step and a choice of voice. Audio-capable multimodal model. How it works: You send the spoken prompt (audio) directly to a deployed model that supports audio input and read its reply. When: Simpler flow, fewer parts; needs a model deployed with audio support.

1.title: Responding to spoken prompts with a multimodal model, continued
1.text: Responding to spoken prompts with a multimodal model. The model must be deployed in your project (Module seven), and your app uses the deployment name like any other model call. Which models support audio input changes often, so always check the model's capabilities in the catalog. Exam tip: "Respond to a spoken question" to either speech to text plus model plus text to speech or an audio-capable multimodal model. The deciding word is "deployed multimodal model": it takes audio in without a separate transcription step.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors writes a program that sends customer reviews to Azure Language and prints whether each is positive or negative. Which call fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: analyze sentiment. analyze sentiment is the text analysis method for sentiment.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Where should the program read the Language key and endpoint from, to avoid hard-coding secrets? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Environment variables. The quickstart reads the key and endpoint from environment variables.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. In the speech sample, which object decides that the audio comes from the microphone? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Audio Config. Audio Config defines the audio source, here the default microphone.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which object turns spoken audio into text? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Speech Recognizer. The speech recognizer performs speech-to-text.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A team wants users to speak a question and hear a spoken answer, using one text model. Which pipeline fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Speech to text, then the text model, then text to speech. Recognition converts speech to text for the model, and synthesis speaks the answer.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. What does a deployed multimodal model that supports audio input allow? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Sending the spoken prompt directly to the model. An audio-capable multimodal model accepts audio as input without a separate transcription step.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which client class is used for text analysis in the sample? Answer: Text Analytics Client. Question two. What does show opinion mining add? Answer: Opinions linked to specific targets in the text. Question three. What does Speech Config hold? Answer: The Speech resource key and endpoint, and the language or voice.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which object defines microphone or file input? Answer: Audio Config. Question five. How long can recognize once async listen? Answer: Up to about thirty seconds, or until silence is detected. Question six. What does S S M L adjust? Answer: Pitch, pronunciation, speaking rate and volume of synthesized speech.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Text analysis app: key and endpoint from environment variables; Text Analytics Client; analyze sentiment(documents, show opinion mining equals True). Speech app: azure-cognitiveservices-speech; Speech Config (resource, language); Audio Config (microphone or file); Speech Recognizer; recognize once async. Text to speech: synthesizer plus a voice; S S M L for pitch, rate, volume. Spoken prompts: pipeline (speech to text, model, text to speech) or an audio-capable multimodal model. In the next module, we continue the course.
